title: ReadKinetic – a free, local-first speed reader for your own books
claim: Show HN: ReadKinetic – a free, local-first speed reader for your own books
why_good: A free, local-first speed reader for your own books — a focused utility for a real habit (faster reading), privacy-friendly.
value: Freemium: a paid sync/library/stats tier for avid readers; hard to charge much for reading UX alone.
risk: Speed-reading is a small, skeptical niche; browser extensions and apps already do this free.

zh.claim: Show HN: ReadKinetic —— 免费、本地优先的、读你自己书的速读器。
zh.why_good: 一个免费、本地优先、读你自己书的速读器——针对真实习惯(读更快)的聚焦小工具,且隐私友好。
zh.value: 免费增值:给爱读者卖付费同步/书库/统计档;光靠阅读体验很难收多少钱。
zh.risk: 速读是个小而存疑的细分;浏览器插件和 app 已经免费做了。
zh.gap: 缺口说不出口。速读工具在每个浏览器里都免费，而产物是一个阅读界面——不是读者能带走的成品。
zh.counter: 一个几十年的老品类，效果本身有争议，且早已作为插件免费送出。这里没有任何一件事是「现在才可能」。

voices.quote: …hen use the tool for the prose. It’s not really fixable at the format level too, there is no good way of showing a person a graph word by word. I suppose what I really should add is some kind of flag to say there was a figure here…

gap: There is no gap that can be said out loud. Speed-reading tools are free in every browser, and the deliverable is a reading interface — not a finished thing the reader walks away with.
counter: A decades-old category with contested evidence behind it, already given away free as extensions. Nothing here is newly possible.
consumer_angle: A reader — but what they receive is a viewer, not an artefact. Kept as archive, not front page.
